ORCA · VISUAL REVIEW · SYNTHETIC MAIL ONLY

Less interface. More conversation.

One review of the current #237 reader, three quieter navigation options, and the #236 design foundation. Current screenshots are actual implementation evidence. A–C are static, design-only previews—not production changes.

Recommendation: A. Replace the large controls with a quiet history divider and contextual jumps. Keep Expand all / Collapse all in an accessible ⋯ menu. All proposed controls retain 44px tap targets. At first unread, omit the redundant unread jump; show “Jump to unread” only after moving away. Show “Jump to latest” only while newest is offscreen.

Actual implementation

Prominent First unread, Newest and Expand all buttons, plus a full-width earlier-message button.

A · Quiet divider

Recommended · proposed

Least visual weight. Earlier messages becomes a divider; jumps appear only away from their destination; Expand all moves into ⋯. Tradeoff: bulk controls require one extra tap.

B · Utility row

Proposed · not implemented

A consistent place for unread status, Latest and ⋯. Easier to discover and scan. Tradeoff: the row always takes space even when the reader needs no help.

C · Position navigator

Proposed · not implemented

Earlier, 22 of 24 and Latest form a compact navigator. Strong orientation in long threads. Tradeoff: numbers and navigation remain prominent.

Desktop detail and overflow behavior

Same synthetic conversation, opened at message 22—the first unread. Earlier content is retained. The drawings focus on navigation; message-body metadata is simplified in the mockups.

#236 · The design foundation

#236 is the earlier design-only exploration. It established visible attention groups and a readable long-thread structure; #237 implements that direction in production web and iOS code, but remains a draft. The button alternatives above are a new proposal layered on that foundation.

What it changes: named attention groups with dates inside each group; clear separation of destination and attention; collapsible sender/time/recipient cards; first-unread or latest entry; conservative quoted-history folding with complete-original recovery.

Why: its synthetic 24-message baseline rendered every body open, producing a 25,853px desktop thread. Hidden attention badges made older Focus mail above newer Normal mail look incorrectly sorted. Existing Notify → Focus → Normal → Quiet → Hidden semantics were retained.

Native iOS · reader

Standalone SwiftUI design app; not a release build.

#236 uses synthetic fixtures. Its native attachment behavior was metadata-only and sending was disabled. It did not establish production HTML/link/attachment parity or complete VoiceOver/Dynamic Type coverage. Those design-stage limitations must not be mistaken for implementation verification.

What stays unchanged

This review changes no production files, attention semantics, read state, links, attachments, branches or releases. The navigation previews are illustrative; their jump buttons do not operate on mail. The overflow disclosure can be opened in the separate static source preview, while this gallery presents captured pixels.
